body.text:
ñ1.1 evaṃ mayā śru[tam eka{smin}?] samaye bhagavāṃ cchrāvastyāṃ viharati sma, karī[ṭe ma]ṇḍalavāṭe\var{karī[ṭema]ṇḍalavāṭe\lem \cod; karī[ma]ṇḍale ca \Dutt} /
ñ1.2 atha khalv āryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisa[ttvo] mahāsattvo 'nekavidyādharakoṭīniyutaśatasaha[sreṇa] parivṛto yena bhagavāṃs tenopasamakrāmad
ñ1.3 upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavantaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtvā\var{#kṛtvā\lem \cod; #kṛtya \Dutt} <e>kānte nyasīda bhagavantam etad avocat /
ñ1.4 idaṃ mama bhagavann ekādaśamukhaṃ nāma hṛdayam ekādaśabhi<x> [kalpako]ṭībhir bhāṣitam /
ñ1.5 ahaṃ caitarhi\var{caitarhi\lem \cod; cet tarhi \Dutt} bhāṣiṣyāmi sarva[sattvānā]m arthāya hitāya sukhāya sarvavyādhipraśa[ma]nāya{ḥ} sarvapāpālakṣmīduḥsvapnapratinivāraṇāya sarvākālamṛtyupratinivāraṇāya aprasādānāṃ prasādanāya sarvavighnavināyakānāṃ praśamanāya /
ñ1.6 nā[haṃ] bhagava(n/t) samanupaśyāmi sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake saśramaṇabrāhmaṇikāyā<ḥ> prajāyā, yad anena hṛdayena rakṣe kṛte paritre parigra[he śā]ntisvastyayane daṇḍaparihare śastraparihare viṣadūṣaṇe\var{viṣa[dūṣa]ṇe \em \Hidas; viṣa[prahā]ṇe \em\Dutt} kṛte yaḥ kaś cid atikrame<n> na praśame<n>, nedaṃ [sthā]na<ṃ> vidyate; sthāpya paurāṇāṃ karma vipacyat<e> tad asya ca kalpayato 'bhiśraddadhataḥ sarveṇa sarvaṃ na bhaviṣyati /
ñ1.8 sarvabuddhastutaḥ samanvāhṛto 'yaṃ hṛdaya<ṃ>. sarvatathāgatānumodito 'yaṃ hṛdayaṃ\var{hṛdayaṃ\lem \em; hṛdaye \cod}/
ñ1.9 smarāmy ahaṃ bhagavaṃ gaṅgānadībālukāsamānāṃ kalpānāṃ pareṇa śatapadmanayanacūḍā\var{#cūḍā#\lem \cod; #cūḍa# \Dutt}pratihatasaṅgavelāma\var{#saṃgavelāma**#\lem \cod; #raṅgavelakiraṇa# \Dutt}rājā\var{rājā\lem \cod; rājasya \em \Dutt} nāma tathāgata{ta}sya{ā} /
ñ1.10 mayā tathāgatasyānti[ke] anuśrutenāyaṃ\var{anuśrutenāyaṃ\lem \em\Ken; śrutam ayaṃ \Dutt} hṛdayam udgṛhītaṃ\var{udgṛhītaṃ\lem \cod; udgṛhītaṃ ca \Dutt} / saha pratilaṃbhe[na] daśasu dikṣu sarvatathāgatā<ḥ> sumukhībhūtā anutpattikadharmakṣāntipratilabdhāḥ /
ñ1.11 evaṃ bahukaro 'yaṃ mā\ill*hṛdayaṃ tasmāt tarhi śrāddhena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā satkṛtyāyaṃ hṛdayaṃ sādhayitavya{ṇa}m / ananyamanasā nityaṃ sādhayitavyaṃ /
ñ1.12 kālyam\var{kālyam\lem \cod; kalyam \Dutt} utthāya aṣṭo<t>taraṃ vāraśataṃ pravartayitavyam /
ñ1.13 dṛṣṭadharmikā guṇā daśa parigrahīyāḥ\var{parigrahīyāḥ\lem \cod; parigrahītavyāḥ\Dutt \em} /
ñ1.14 katame daśa{ḥ} ?
ñ1.15 [1] yad uta nirvyādhir bhaviṣyati /
ñ1.16 [2] sarvata<thāgataiḥ> parigṛhītaś ca bhaviṣyati /
ñ1.17 [3] dhanadhānyahiraṇyasaṃbharaṇam\var{#saṃbharaṇam\em \Hidas ābharaṇaṃ \em \Dutt} asya akṣayaṃ bhaviṣyati /
ñ1.18 [4] sarvaśatravo vaśyā avamarditā bhaviṣyanti /
ñ1.19 [5] rājasabhāyāṃ\var{#sabhā\lem \cod; #sabhāyāṃ \Dutt} prathamam ālaṃbitavyaṃ\var{ālaṃbitavyaṃ\lem \cod; ālapitavyaṃ \Dutt} maṃsyati /
ñ1.20 [6] na viṣaṃ na garam na jvaraṃ na śastram kāye kramiṣyati /
ñ1.21 [7] nodakena kālaṃ kariṣyati /
ñ1.22 [8] nāgninā kālaṃ kariṣyati /
ñ1.23 [9] nākālamṛtyunā kālaṃ\var{kālaṃ\lem \cod; kālaṃ ca \Dutt} kariṣyati / %NB number 10 seems to be missing, or a different counting is required
ñ1.24 apare catvāro guṇānuśaṃsā udgrahīṣyati /
ñ1.25 [1] maraṇakāle tathā[gatada]rśanaṃ bhaviṣyati /
ñ1.26 [2] na cāpāyeṣūpapatsyate /
ñ1.27 [3] na [viṣamā]parihāreṇa kālaṃ kariṣyati /
ñ1.28 [4] itaś c<y>utaḥ sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāv upapatsyate
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the <s>Karīṭa</s> circular enclosure. Then the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the great being, surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of <s>vidyādharas</s> (knowledge-holders), approached the <s>Bhagavat</s>. Having approached and bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavat</s>, and having circumambulated the <s>Bhagavat</s>, he sat down to one side and addressed the <s>Bhagavat</s> thus: 'This, O <s>Bhagavat</s>, is my <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart-dhāraṇī) called <s>Ekādaśamukha</s> (Eleven-Faced), which was spoken over eleven <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons). And I shall now speak it for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of all beings, for the pacification of all diseases, for the warding off of all misfortune, bad omens, and evil dreams, for the prevention of all untimely death, for the gladdening of those without faith, and for the pacification of all obstacles and <s>Vināyakas</s> (obstructing demons). I do not see, O <s>Bhagavat</s>, in this world with its <s>devas</s>, <s>Māra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, with its <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, any being who, when this <s>hṛdaya</s> has been employed for protection, safekeeping, guarding, peace, well-being, removal of punishment, removal of weapons, and neutralization of poison, would not be pacified by any transgression — such a case does not exist; except for the ripening of former <s>karma</s> — but even that, for one who practices [this dhāraṇī] with full faith, will entirely cease to be. This <s>hṛdaya</s> has been praised by all <s>Buddhas</s>, approved by all <s>Buddhas</s>. This <s>hṛdaya</s> has been rejoiced in by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. I remember, O <s>Bhagavat</s>, beyond <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Śatapadmanayanacūḍāpratihatasaṅgavelāmarāja</s>. This <s>hṛdaya</s> was received by me, having heard it in the presence of that <s>Tathāgata</s>. Simultaneously with its attainment, all the <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the ten directions became favorably disposed and attained <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (the acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas). So beneficial is this <s>hṛdaya</s>; therefore it should be practiced with respect by a faithful son or daughter of good family. It should be practiced constantly, with undivided mind. Rising early in the morning, one should recite it one hundred and eight times. Ten benefits visible in this very life should be obtained. Which ten? (1) One will be free from disease. (2) One will be protected by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. (3) One's wealth, grain, gold, and possessions will be inexhaustible. (4) All enemies will be subdued and vanquished. (5) One will be considered the first to be addressed in the king's assembly. (6) Neither poison, nor harmful substances, nor fever, nor weapons will enter one's body. (7) One will not die by water. (8) One will not die by fire. (9) One will not die by untimely death. Furthermore, four additional benefits and advantages will be obtained: (1) At the time of death, there will be a vision of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. (2) One will not be reborn in the lower realms (<s>apāya</s>). (3) One will not die through adverse circumstances. (4) Having departed from here, one will be reborn in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (the Land of Bliss).'

body.text:
smarāmy ahaṃ bhagavann it daśānāṃ gaṅgānadībāl[u]kāsamānāṃ kalpānāṃ tataḥ pareṇa paratareṇa mandāravagandho nāma tathāgato 'bhūt{a} /
tatra mayā gṛhaparibhūtenāyam udgṛhīta<m> /
catvāriṃśat kalpasahasrāṇi saṃsārāḥ paścānmukhīkṛtāḥ\var{#kṛtāḥ\lem \em\Dutt; #kṛtāṇi \cod} /

children.text: eṣa ca mayā hṛdayaṃ pravartitvā sarvabuddhānāṃ\var{sarvabuddhānāṃ\conj \Nagashima; sarvasmin \Dutt} karuṇāyanajñānagarbhabodhisattvavimokṣaṃ pra[tila]bdham / \marginpar{\Dutt p.38}
children.translated_text: And by me, having set forth this <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart-dhāraṇī), the <s>Bodhisattva</s> liberation of the womb of compassion-knowledge of all <s>Buddhas</s> (<s>karuṇāyanajñānagarbhabodhisattvavimokṣa</s>) was obtained.

children.text:
yena\var{ye\lem \Dutt; yena \cod} bandhanabaddhā ye vadhyaprāptā\var{ye\rarr badhyaprāptā repeated \dittography \cod} ye udakāgnivividhaduḥkhābhyāhatā<ḥ> tad anenāhaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ layanaṃ trāṇam śaraṇam parāyaṇaṃ bhavāmi yat\var{yat\lem \Dutt; yaḥ \cod} /
sarvaduṣṭayakṣarākṣasānām anayā hṛdayeṇā\var{anayā hṛdayeṇā\lem \cod\hybrid; anena hṛdayena \Dutt} karṣitvā maitracittā[n] dayācittān\var{dayācittān\lem \Dutt; dayācittādayācittān \cod} kṛtvānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratiṣṭhāpayāmi /
evaṃ mahārthiko\var{mahārthiko\lem \cod; mahārdhiko \Dutt} 'yaṃ mama bhagavat hṛ[dayam] ekavelāṃ prakāśitvā catvāro mūlāpattayaḥ kṣa[yaṃ] gacchanti\var{gacchanti\lem \Dutt; gakṣanti \cod} .
 pañcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi niravaya<va>ṃ tanvīkariṣya<n>ti /
kaḥ punar vādo yathābhāṣitaṃ pratipatsyanti / % Dutt supplies ``teṣāṃ ye'' but better understand: ``why say more, these will happen as they are taught''
children.translated_text:
Those who are bound in chains, those who have reached the point of execution, those who are struck by the manifold sufferings of water, fire, and other calamities — by this [<s>hṛdaya</s>], I become the refuge, protection, shelter, and ultimate resort of all beings.
By this <s>hṛdaya</s>, having drawn in all hostile <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s>, making them possess minds of friendliness and compassion, I establish them in unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).
So great is the purpose of this my <s>hṛdaya</s>, O <s>Bhagavat</s>: by proclaiming it even once, the four root transgressions (<s>mūlāpattis</s>) are destroyed.
The five acts of immediate retribution (<s>ānantarya karmas</s>) are made utterly thin.
What more need be said? All shall come to pass as it is taught.

body.translated_text:
I remember, O <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One), that beyond ten <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river, and still further beyond, there was a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Mandāravagandha</s> (Fragrance of the Mandāra Flower).
There, by me, while still a householder, this [<s>hṛdaya</s>] was taken up.
Forty thousand <s>kalpas</s> of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) were turned backwards.

body.text:
%sandhi dissolved from here on
aneka-buddha-śata-sahasra-avaropita-kuśala-mūlā bhaviṣyanti\var{mūlā bhaviṣyanti\lem \cod; #mūlaṃ bhaviṣyati \Dutt} ye śroṣyanti prāk- eva japa-sādhana-ādibhiḥ /% prāg eva: ``how much more...''
sarva-manoratham- paripūrayiṣyāmi .
ye ca\var{ye ca\lem \em; yaśca \cod} caturdaśīpañcadaśī\com{dual loc. hybrid? \Dutt: ``should be caturdaśyāṃ pañcadaśyāṃ''.} mām- uddiśya- upavasante\var{upavasante \cod; upavasati \Dutt} {/}
catvāriṃśa<t> kalpa-sahasrāṇi saṃsārā<n> paścāt-mukhīkariṣyanti /
tena nā[madhe]yam- api grahaṇena bhagavan- saha sas- ayam- buddha-koṭī-niyuta-śata-sahasra-atireka-samam /
mama nāmadheya-grahaṇena [sa]rva-sattvās- avaivartikatvaṃ prasavanti{ḥ} /
sarvavyādhibhis- parimucyante\var{parimucyante\lem \cod; parimucyate \Dutt} /
sarva-āvaraṇebhya[s-] sarva-bhayebhyas- sarva-kāya-vāk-manas-duścaritebhyas- parimokṣyante /

children.text: teṣām- eva kara-tala-gatā- buddha-bodhis- bhaviṣyati /\marginpar{\Dutt p.39}
children.translated_text: For them, the awakening of a <s>Buddha</s> shall be as if placed in the palm of their hand.

children.text:
bhagavān āha /
sādhu sādhu kula-putra yat te\var{yat te\lem \cod; yat \Dutt} sarva-sattvānām- antike- evam-rūpā\var{evaṃrūpā\lem \Dutt; evaṃrūpaṃ} mahā-karuṇā /
śakṣyasi tvaṃ kula-putra\var{kulaputra\lem \em; kulaputraḥ \Dutt} anena- upāyena {sarva}sarva-sattvānā[m- anuttarā]yāṃ\var{sattvānām\lem \Dutt; sattvān* \cod} samyak-saṃbodhau pratiṣṭhāpayitum / udgṛhītam- ca\var{udgṛhīto yaṃ \cod} [mayā] hṛdayam- anumoditam /
children.translated_text:
The <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One) said: 'Well done, well done, O son of good family! That you have such great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) toward all beings!
You are able, O son of good family, by this skillful means (<s>upāya</s>), to establish all beings in unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).
And this <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart-dhāraṇī) has been taken up and approved by me.
Speak, O son of good family!'

children.text: tatra\var{tatra\lem \cod; tataḥ \Dutt} khalu- āryāvalokiteśvaras- bodhisattvo\var{bodhisattva \Dutt} utthāya- āsanāt- eka-aṃsam- uttara-āsaṅgam- kṛtvā bhagavatas- caraṇayos- praṇipatya{m} idam- hṛdayam- āvartayati sma //
children.translated_text: Thereupon the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, prostrating at the feet of the <s>Bhagavat</s>, recited this <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart-dhāraṇī):

body.translated_text:
Those who shall hear it will come to have wholesome roots planted with many hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s> — how much more so through <s>japa</s> (recitation), <s>sādhana</s> (practice), and so forth!
I shall fulfill all their heart's desires.
And those who observe a fast dedicated to me on the fourteenth and fifteenth days [of the lunar month] will turn back forty thousand <s>kalpas</s> of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
By the mere taking of that name, O <s>Bhagavat</s>, it is equal to and surpasses the merit of many hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>.
By taking my name, all beings attain the state of non-regression (<s>avaivartika</s>).
They are freed from all diseases.
They shall be liberated from all obscurations, all fears, and all misconduct of body, speech, and mind.

body.text:
namas- ratnatrayāya /
namas- vairocanāya tathāgatāya /
namas-āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahā-kāruṇikāya{ḥ} /
namas-\var{nama\lem \em; namaḥ \cod\Dutt} atīta-anāgata-pratyutpa[nnebhyaḥ]\var{missing in Chinese 1071} sarva-tathāgatebhyas- arhadbhyaḥ samyak-saṃbuddhebhyaḥ /
body.translated_text:
Homage to the <s>Triratna</s> (Three Jewels).
Homage to <s>Vairocana</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>.
Homage to the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the <s>Mahāsattva</s>, the Great Compassionate One.
Homage to all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones of the past, future, and present.

body.text:
oṃ diri diri\var{diri diri\lem \em; dhara dhara dhiri dhiri \Dutt from Tib} / dhuru dhuru / iṭṭe viṭṭe / cale cale / pracale pracale / [kusume]\var{kusume\em supplied from Tib also in Chinese} kusumavare / ili mili ciṭi\var{ciṭi\lem \cod; viṭi \Dutt} svāhā /
evam-\var{eṣa\lem evaṃ \Dutt} mūla-mantra[s-] //
body.translated_text:
<s>Oṃ diri diri / dhuru dhuru / iṭṭe viṭṭe / cale cale / pracale pracale / kusume kusumavare / ili mili ciṭi svāhā</s>.
Thus is the root <s>mantra</s> (<s>mūlamantra</s>).

body.text:
namas- ratna-trayāya /
namas- āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya /
tat- yathā ha ha ha ha\var{ha ha ha ha\lem \cod; hā [hā hā] hā \Dutt} / ime tile cile bhile khile svāhā /
snāna-upaspṛśana\var{#opaspṛśana#\lem \cod; #opasparśana# \Dutt}-vastra-abhyukṣipaṇa-mantras- sapta-jāpena /\com{abhyukṣipaṇa-\lem BHS for abhyukṣaṇa- or confused with \dhatu{kṣip-}.}
body.translated_text:
Homage to the <s>Triratna</s>.
Homage to the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the <s>Mahāsattva</s>.
That is to say: <s>ha ha ha ha / ime tile cile bhile khile svāhā</s>.
This is the <s>mantra</s> for bathing, sprinkling, and offering garments—to be recited with seven repetitions.

body.text:
namas- ratna-trayāya /
namas- āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvā[ya ma]hāsattvāya /
tat- yathā ṭuru ṭuru ha ha ha ha\var{ha ha ha ha\lem \cod; hā hā hā hā \Dutt} svāhā /
dhū[pa-dī]pa-nivedana-mantraḥ /
body.translated_text:
Homage to the <s>Triratna</s>.
Homage to the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the <s>Mahāsattva</s>.
That is to say: <s>ṭuru ṭuru ha ha ha ha svāhā</s>.
This is the <s>mantra</s> for offering incense and lamps.

body.text:
namas- ratna-trayāya /
namas- āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya /
tat- yathā siri siri dhiri dhiri siri dhiri\var{siri siri \lem \em based on Chinese; thiri thiri \Dutt} svāhā /
gandha-puṣpa-<*>upanivedana-mantras- /
body.translated_text:
Homage to the <s>Triratna</s>.
Homage to the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the <s>Mahāsattva</s>.
That is to say: <s>siri siri dhiri dhiri siri dhiri svāhā</s>.
This is the <s>mantra</s> for offering perfume and flowers.

body.text:
namas- ratna-trayāya /
namas- āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahā-karuṇikāya /
tat- yathā sāde sāde / sidi sidi / sudu sudu svāhā /
bali-nivedana-mantras- eka-viṃśati-japena /
body.translated_text:
Homage to the <s>Triratna</s>.
Homage to the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the <s>Mahāsattva</s>, the Great Compassionate One.
That is to say: <s>sāde sāde / sidi sidi / sudu sudu svāhā</s>.
This is the <s>mantra</s> for the <s>bali</s> (food-offering)—to be recited with twenty-one repetitions.

body.text:
namas- ratna-trayāya /
namas- āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya / mahā-karuṇikāya /
tat- yathā masi\var{masi\lem \cod; yasi \Dutt}ddhasi cari huru icuruḥ suruḥ suru\var{suru\lem \cod; muruḥ \Dutt} svāhā /
homa-mantras- /
anena mantreṇa jātīkāṣṭhair\var{jātīkāṣṭhair\lem \cod; jñātinaṣṭais \Dutt} agnim- prajvālya dadhi-madhu-ghṛta-abhyaktānām- ahorātra-uṣitena- ekena triṃśatā homa<s-> kāryaḥ /
tatas- karmaṃ\var{karmaṃ\lem \cod BH; karma \Dutt} samārabhet /
body.translated_text:
Homage to the <s>Triratna</s>.
Homage to the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the <s>Mahāsattva</s>, the Great Compassionate One.
That is to say: <s>masiddhasi cari huru icuruḥ suruḥ suru svāhā</s>.
This is the <s>homa</s> (fire-offering) <s>mantra</s>.
With this <s>mantra</s>, having lit a fire with <s>jātī</s> (jasmine) wood, with [fuel] anointed with curds, honey, and ghee, after keeping vigil for a day and night, one should perform thirty <s>homas</s>.
Then one should commence the ritual.

body.text:
namas- ratna-trayāya /
namas- āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahā-karuṇikāya /
tat- yathā ili mili pili\var{pili\lem from Chinese; \omitted \Dutt} tili / tili hili svāhā /
diśābandhas-\var{diśābandha\lem \em; dīpābaddha \Dutt} udakena sarṣapair vā\var{sarṣapair vā\lem \em \Nagashima based on Chinese} bhasmanā vā sapta-jāpena /
body.translated_text:
Homage to the <s>Triratna</s>.
Homage to the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the <s>Mahāsattva</s>, the Great Compassionate One.
That is to say: <s>ili mili pili tili / tili hili svāhā</s>.
For binding the directions (<s>diśābandha</s>)—with water, mustard seeds, or ashes, to be recited seven times.

body.text:
namas- ratna-trayāya /
[na]mas- āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya / mahā-karuṇikāya /
tat- yathā piṭi piṭi tiṭi tiṭi / viṭi\var{viṭi viṭi\lem \cod; siṭi siṭi viṭi viṭi Chinese} viṭi gaccha gaccha bhagavan-\var{bhagavan\lem \em (illegible in photo); bhagavān \Dutt} āryāvalokiteśvara sva-bhavanam- sva-bhavanam- svāhā /

children.text: udake sapta-vārā<n> parijapya caturdiśam- kṣipe\com{kṣipe\lem \cod; kṣipet \Dutt; the MSS's reading should mean that the sādhaka speaks these words as part of the mantra} /
children.translated_text: Having recited seven times over water, one should cast it in the four directions.
O noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, go to your own abode.

body.translated_text:
Homage to the <s>Triratna</s>.
Homage to the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the <s>Mahāsattva</s>, the Great Compassionate One.
That is to say: <s>piṭi piṭi tiṭi tiṭi / viṭi viṭi gaccha gaccha</s> O <s>Bhagavat</s> noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, to your own abode, to your own abode, <s>svāhā</s>.

body.text: oṃ namo ratnatrāyāyaḥ namaś caṇḍavajrapāṇa{ā}ye mahāśaktasenāpa<ta>ye . tad yathā ugrāya svāhā // ati ugrāya svāhā // ugrapriyāya svāhā ugrapriyāya svāhā .
body.translated_text: Oṃ. Homage to the Three Jewels (<s>Ratnatraya</s>)! Homage to <s>Caṇḍavajrapāṇi</s> (the Fierce Vajra-Holder), the great and mighty commander! That is to say: To the Fierce One, <s>svāhā</s>! To the Exceedingly Fierce One, <s>svāhā</s>! To the Beloved of the Fierce One, <s>svāhā</s>! To the Beloved of the Fierce One, <s>svāhā</s>!
[Editorial note: possibly derived from '<s>rudrapriya</s>' (beloved of <s>Rudra</s>) etc.]
